summary: Los Padres lookout in Santa Barbara County; its 1965 cab is stripped and vandalized, unstaffed, and a 2025 refurbishment project is suspended.

facts.design: Current structure: 13 by 13 foot CL-100 metal cab on a 12 foot concrete block base, installed 1965

access.note: The 2020 register visit found the approach road behind a locked gate. A Forest Service page lists the adjacent day-use site as open daily and year-round, which the two sources do not reconcile.

events.note: Forest Service lookout station moved from Zaca Peak to the summit of Figueroa Mountain
Construction of a new station begun; a newspaper said the planned building would be mostly glass; completion not confirmed in sources read
Zolla Ontiveros in charge of the lookout on Figueroa Mountain (December 1926 item)
Z. A. Ontiveros left for the summer season as lookout
Zollo Ontiveros began his 15th consecutive year as lookout (June 1931 item)
William Green announced as starting lookout; last staffing item in the history page read
Original C3 cab on a timber tower replaced by a 13 by 13 foot CL-100 metal cab on a 12 foot concrete block base
Registered June 19, 2010; nominated by Brad Eells
November 11, 2020 register visit: windows broken, furnishings destroyed, door secured with a chain, debris cleared by the Forest Service
November 9, 2022 inspection with the acting district ranger; discussed refurbishing
January 21, 2025 on-site meeting with the district ranger and archaeologists about refurbishing the stripped-out cab; project suspended

notes_for_editor: The record's height_m 152.4 (500 ft) is not supported by any source read: the register gives no height, and the history page gives none. It looks wrong for a cab on a 12-foot base. Left out of facts. Not added to corrections because no sourced proposed value exists; a human should check and remove or correct it. Record kind two_story was not checked against a source. Unresolved conflicts: (a) cab model, the register description says CL-100 while a photo caption says CL-30; the story uses CL-100. (b) Access: the 2020 register visit found a locked gate on the approach road, while the Forest Service day-use page lists the site as open daily and year-round. The FFLA project page linked in search returned 404, so it was not used. (c) Completion of the 1922 station is not confirmed in sources read. (d) The end of staffing, presumably the 1970s, is the register's estimate, not a dated record. The 2025 report's account of the federal workforce cuts is the chapter's own explanation; the story attributes it to the report. Fact check 2026-10-08: the 2025 report dates the meeting 1/21/25 but also calls it Inauguration Day, which was January 20, 2025; the story says only January 2025 and attributes the day to the report. The summit wording comes from a 1922 trail item, not the register. The Ontiveros name is printed as Zolla, Tollo, Zollo and Z. A.; the story uses Zollo Ontiveros and names the Z. A. form. The day-use page does not describe the tower as open to visitors, so the story says only that. No new photos. Budget: register, Forest Lookouts page, 2022 and 2025 chapter reports, and the Forest Service day-use page; one search.
